Jennifer Lindahl Bonnie Bolden Fernando Cervantes Jr.

Montgomery Advertiser

Updated Sept. 3, 2026, 1:50 p.m. CT

President Donald Trump’s approval rating among Alabama voters has slipped in recent weeks, according to the latest Civiqs polling, even as he continues to hold a positive overall rating in the state.

Nationally, 35 percent of voters approve of Trump's job performance while 59 percent disapprove as of August 19, leaving him significantly underwater with a net approval rating of -24, according to Civiqs' rolling online tracking poll of registered voters. The survey has garnered 124,759 responses since January 20, 2025, when Trump was inaugurated for a second term. [...] In Indiana, Trump's net approval rating slipped underwater in Civiqs' polling in late June, after being positive throughout his second term. It now stands at -3.

Trump has a 45% approval rating in Mississippi, according to Aug. 31 polling data from Civiqs. That's the lowest ever for the state.

His disapproval rating is 49%, which is also the highest for both terms. About 6% neither approve nor disapprove.

Trump started this term in 2025 with about a 56% approval rating in the Magnolia State. About 41% disapproved. Both groups basically mirrored each other for most of his second term, inching closer and closer together over time.
